policy: Clarity, concision and specificity are useful across genres.
Assess first person, passive voice and sentence length by their purpose, not automatic penalties.
Show rather than tell applies selectively to narrative; analytical writing must explain its inferences.
Keep analysis, evidence, organization and mechanics scores independent.
Do not map percentages into missing 1–4 criterion labels.

pairs.less_preferred: The weather outside was really bad and cold. It started to rain heavily. I walked fast to get home because I didn’t want to get soaking wet. My clothes got all wet anyway and I was shivering so much. It was a very miserable day.
pairs.preferred: A slate-grey sky pressed down on the pavement as icy droplets hammered the gutters. I pulled my collar tight and broke into a sprint, chasing the amber glow of my front porch, though the autumn chill had already soaked through my coat.
preference_reasons: Concrete sensory detail rather than generic labels.
Purposeful sentence variation and specific verbs.
limitations: Narrative style preference, not evidence of analytical reasoning.
A concise, plain narrative can also be strong; imagery is not mandatory in every genre.

pairs.less_preferred: In this essay, I am going to talk about why social media is bad for teenagers. Social media makes teens feel bad about themselves because they see pictures of other people looking perfect. A lot of studies show that social media causes depression. Therefore, we should probably try to spend less time on our phones.
pairs.preferred: Unrelenting exposure to curated digital feeds fosters chronic social comparison among adolescents. Rather than merely documenting reality, platforms like Instagram prompt users to measure their lived experiences against idealized highlights, a dynamic increasingly linked to rising rates of adolescent anxiety and depressive symptoms.
preference_reasons: A focused assertion rather than an announcement.
A more explicit proposed mechanism connecting comparison and distress.
More precise description of the proposed relationship.
limitations: Neither paragraph supplies studies, source text, or independently checkable evidence.
Preferred prose does not justify a high evidence or source-accuracy grade.
Causation and empirical associations require evidence; a confident tone cannot establish them.
